File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or SHA1 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or MD5 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or SHA1 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480") or MD5 in~ ("31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["31ecc5939de6d24cf60c50d4ca26cf7a8c322db82a8ce4bd122ebd89cf634255", "b1e4b1f3aad0d489ab0e9208031c67402bbb8480"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — Malicious Release of elementary-data PyPI Package Steals Cloud Credentials from
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("site.py", "__init__.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

| where (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/kubernetes/", "/etc/passwd", "/etc/shadow", "/var/log/auth.log", "/dev/null") or FileName in~ ("site.py", "__init__.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,

      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/kubernetes/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/passwd*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/shadow*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/log/auth.log*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/dev/null*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("site.py","__init__.py"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
High

Qinglong task scheduler RCE vulnerabilities exploited in the wild for cryptomining

Snyk
2026-04-27 9 use cases 1 technique 6 kill-chain phases detected

Two authentication bypass vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-3965, CVE-2026-4047) in the Qinglong task scheduling panel were exploited in the wild to deploy cryptomining malware. Here's what happened, how the attacks worked, and what self-hosted application operators should learn from this incident.

Qinglong CVE-2026-3965 auth bypass via /open/user/init credential reset AIExploitation High
Detects unauthenticated PUT requests to the Qinglong /open/user/init endpoint that reinitialize admin credentials by abusing the Express.js rewrite from /open/* to /api/$1. Hunts the article's exact exploitation request at the reverse-proxy / WAF layer where HTTP path is visible. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact curl proof-of-concept (PUT http://target:5700/open/user/init) and the Express.js rewrite rule documented in Issue #2933. Cross-checked against the Snyk vulnerability DB entry SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732 and GitHub issues #2933 / #2924; the /open/* -> /api/$1 rewrite is the structural primitive and is only legitimately used by anonymous endpoints (login, ping) — never /user/init. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2933 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/pull/2941 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732
ATT&CKT1190 T1556
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate first-boot Qinglong setup hitting /open/user/init during the install wizard
  • Internal blue-team / scanner replay of the published PoC for patch verification
  • Synthetic monitor probing the init endpoint to confirm availability
  • An admin re-running the init flow after factory-resetting the container
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — exclude internal scanner / synthetic monitors and tag known admin source IPs
| where SourceIP !in ("10.10.20.5","10.10.20.6") // synthetic monitor IPs — replace with env
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","OpenVAS")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the SourceIP / RequestClientApplication from the WAF hit, confirm whether the host is a known Qinglong instance, and check whether `qinglong` version is <=2.20.1 (vulnerable). Step 2 (contain): block the SourceIP at the perimeter, force-restart the Qinglong container with QL_ENABLE_TWO_FACTOR=true and rotate the admin credential; if PR #2941 not yet applied, take the panel off the public internet (VPN/SSH-tunnel only). Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the same SourceIP for follow-on /api/system/command-run, /api/crons modifications, DNS queries to file.551911.xyz, and file writes under /ql/data/db/.fullgc within the next 24h.
// Defender XDR cannot observe inbound HTTP request paths to a Linux container app.
// Pivot to follow-on artefact: node (qinglong) process spawning a shell that touches
// the admin auth/config layer shortly after exploitation, OR the Qinglong app restarting
// unexpectedly (config.sh write triggers restart per article).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","pm2","ts-node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("user/init","/open/user","config.sh","auth.db","db/auth")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: WAF / reverse-proxy logs ingested via CommonSecurityLog
let WAFHits = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod in~ ("PUT","POST")
| where RequestURL has "/open/user/init"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct;
// Secondary: Nginx access logs forwarded via Syslog
let NginxHits = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("nginx","openresty","caddy","traefik")
| where SyslogMessage has "/open/user/init"
| where SyslogMessage has_any (" PUT "," POST ")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
union WAFHits, NginxHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Qinglong CVE-2026-3965 Admin Credential Reset via /open/user/init
id: 8a2c7d4e-1f3b-4a5c-9e8d-2b6f4c1a9d50
description: Detects unauthenticated PUT/POST requests to Qinglong's /open/user/init endpoint which abuses an Express.js URL rewrite (/open/* -> /api/$1) to reach the protected admin init endpoint and reset admin credentials.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/qinglong-task-scheduler-rce-vulnerabilities/
  - https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2933
  - https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15440732

falsepositives:
  - Legitimate first-time Qinglong setup from a known admin workstation
  - Synthetic monitoring / health-check probing the init endpoint
level: high
(@http.method:PUT OR @http.method:POST) @http.url_details.path:"/open/user/init"
// Falcon FDR does not capture inbound HTTP request paths on the server.
// Pivot to the post-credential-reset behavioural artefact: node (qinglong) spawning a shell

Qinglong CVE-2026-4047 case-mismatch auth bypass via /aPi/system/command-run AIExploitation High
Detects requests to Qinglong /system/command-run where the URL path uses any mixed-case variant of /api/ (e.g. /aPi/, /Api/, /API/). The middleware uses case-sensitive startsWith('/api/') while Express routes case-insensitively, bypassing auth while still reaching the command-execution endpoint. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim PoC (curl -X PUT 'http://target:5700/aPi/system/command-run') and the case-mismatch primitive described in Issue #2934 — middleware does req.path.startsWith('/api/') while Express routes case-insensitively. Regex /(?i)/api/ combined with negative filter on lowercase /api/ catches every mixed-case bypass without false-positive on the legitimate path. Cross-checked Snyk DB SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15468374 and PR #2941 (the real fix at the middleware layer). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2934 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/pull/2941 • https://security.snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-JS-WHYOURQINGLONG-15468374
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vulnerability scanner (Tenable/Qualys/Nessus) replaying the public PoC against an internal Qinglong instance
  • Internal CTF / red-team exercise targeting a sandboxed Qinglong instance
  • Buggy client library emitting case-randomised URLs (very rare in practice — Express convention is all-lowercase)
  • Patch-validation traffic from a maintenance workstation after upgrading to >=2.20.2
Suppression filter
// Sentinel — strip known scanners and patch-validation IPs
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","OpenVAS","Nuclei","ZAP")
| where SourceIP !in ("10.10.20.5","10.10.20.6") // patch-validation hosts — replace per env
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): confirm the target host runs Qinglong <=2.20.1; pull the full RequestURL and the SourceIP / User-Agent; map the SourceIP against known scanner ranges. Step 2 (contain): block the SourceIP at the WAF/perimeter, immediately upgrade Qinglong past PR #2941 (>=2.20.2), audit /ql/config/config.sh and /ql/data/db for tampering, and rotate any credentials stored in the panel. Step 3 (hunt): for the same victim host, query for outbound DNS to file.551911.xyz, file writes to /ql/data/db/.fullgc, and any process named .fullgc launched with nohup; pivot on the SourceIP across the estate for other Qinglong / open Express panels hit with the same case-mismatch technique.
// Detects the qinglong node process spawning a shell with attacker-supplied command
// when CVE-2026-4047 is exploited against /aPi/system/command-run.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","pm2","ts-node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","curl","wget")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","file.551911.xyz","/ql/data/db/.fullgc","nohup","chmod +x","$(uname","-fsSL")
  or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1\s+&"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: WAF / reverse-proxy logs ingested via CommonSecurityLog
let MixedCaseApi = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL matches regex @"/(?i:api)/(?:system/command-run|system/run-script|crons)"
| where RequestURL !contains "/api/" // exclude the all-lowercase legitimate path
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct;
// Secondary: Nginx access logs forwarded via Syslog
let NginxMixedCase = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("nginx","openresty","caddy","traefik")
| where SyslogMessage matches regex @"/(?i:api)/(?:system/command-run|system/run-script|crons)"
| where SyslogMessage !contains "/api/"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage;
// Tertiary: ASIM process telemetry — qinglong spawning a shell with attacker payload markers
let QinglongShell = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","pm2","ts-node")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("qinglong","/ql/build","/ql/src","@whyour/qinglong")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","/ql/data/db/.fullgc","nohup","chmod +x","$(uname")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine;
union MixedCaseApi, NginxMixedCase, QinglongShell
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Qinglong cryptominer payload download from file.551911.xyz AIDelivery High
Detects DNS resolution or network egress to file.551911.xyz, the unofficial domain hosting platform-specific .fullgc cryptominer binaries (Linux x86_64, ARM64, macOS) dropped after Qinglong auth-bypass exploitation. Domain has no legitimate enterprise use. Rationale: Article identifies file.551911.xyz as the exclusive payload host, with the verbatim shell snippet `u="https://file.551911.xyz/fullgc/$(uname -s)_$(uname -m)"`. Domain has no legitimate enterprise use, is a numeric-prefix .xyz TLD (commodity malware infra pattern), and is named in multiple GitHub Issues (#2923, #2928). Both DNS-layer and process-layer hits are independent high-fidelity signals. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2923 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2928 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2926
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researcher pivoting on the domain from a sandbox
  • Blue-team replay of the article's PoC for detection validation
  • Passive DNS / threat-intel scraper resolving the domain for enrichment
  • Curious admin investigating the article and copy-pasting the URL
Suppression filter
// Defender — exclude known sandbox / threat-research workstations
| where DeviceName !in~ ("sandbox01","ti-research-vm")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("threatintel","sandbox")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the host that resolved file.551911.xyz; confirm Qinglong (Node, port 5700) is running and check version against PR #2941. Step 2 (contain): sinkhole / block file.551911.xyz and the 551911.xyz parent at the DNS/perimeter layer; isolate the affected host; kill any .fullgc process; quarantine /ql/data/db/.fullgc and capture for IR. Step 3 (hunt): hash the recovered binary and pivot across the estate (DeviceFileEvents on the SHA256); search Qinglong config.sh on every Qinglong host in the org for shell injection (curl/wget/nohup patterns); check whether any Nezha monitoring panels managed from the host were also touched (article notes lateral pivot via Nezha).
// DNS / network egress + curl/wget command line referencing the article's exact payload host
let PayloadHost = dynamic(["file.551911.xyz",".551911.xyz"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (PayloadHost) or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)file\.551911\.xyz"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","fetch","aria2c")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","fullgc/Linux","fullgc/Darwin","fullgc/$(uname")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType="ProcessCreated", RemoteUrl=tostring(parse_url(ProcessCommandLine).Host), RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null), InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName;
union NetHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
// DNS resolution to the payload host
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Name has "551911.xyz"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Result;
// ASIM DNS for multi-source coverage
let AsimDns = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has "551911.xyz"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Result=DnsResponseName;
// Process-side: curl/wget on Linux invoking the exact payload URL
let CurlHits = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl","wget","fetch","aria2c")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("file.551911.xyz","fullgc/Linux","fullgc/Darwin")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP="", Name=ActingProcessCommandLine, QueryType="PROCESS", Result=ActingProcessName;
union DnsHits, AsimDns, CurlHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hidden .fullgc cryptominer binary written to /ql/data/db/ AIInstallation High
Detects file creation of /ql/data/db/.fullgc - the article's exact dropper path for the Qinglong cryptominer, deliberately named to masquerade as a JVM Full Garbage Collection process. The leading dot hides it from default `ls`, and the path piggybacks on Qinglong's data directory. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim payload-drop path `/ql/data/db/.fullgc` (Block snippet `b="/ql/data/db/.fullgc"`). Dot-prefix + Qinglong-specific data dir + filename masquerading as Full GC = three independent high-fidelity signals on a single file path. Cross-checked against GitHub Issues #2923 (first report) and #2928 (detailed report) - both name the exact path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2923 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2928
ATT&CKT1105 T1564.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR engineer copying the recovered binary back to /ql/data/db/.fullgc during forensic reconstruction
  • Detection-validation lab dropping a benign file at the same path to test the rule
  • Backup-restore operation rehydrating a previously-infected snapshot
  • Honeypot deliberately exposing a vulnerable Qinglong instance
Suppression filter
// Defender - exclude IR-reconstruction hosts
| where DeviceName !in~ ("ir-forensics-01","detection-lab-vm")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("ir-team","detection-eng")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the SHA256 from DeviceFileEvents, check VT/Intezer for known cryptominer-family hits, identify the InitiatingProcess that wrote the file (expect curl/wget invoked from a node-spawned shell). Step 2 (contain): isolate the host, kill any running .fullgc process (see UC5), quarantine the binary, revert /ql/config/config.sh to a known-good copy (check git history for shell injection from the attacker), upgrade Qinglong past PR #2941. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the binary SHA256 across the org (DeviceFileEvents); search for the same shell-injection pattern in other Qinglong instances' config.sh; check Nezha monitoring panels managed from this host for compromise (article-noted lateral pivot); search WAF logs for the originating /open/user/init or /aPi/system/command-run hit (UC1/UC2).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has "/ql/data/db" and FileName == ".fullgc")
   or FolderPath endswith "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or FileName == ".fullgc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// ASIM file-events - primary path
let FileHits = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath endswith "/ql/data/db/.fullgc")
   or (TargetFilePath has "/ql/data/db" and TargetFileName == ".fullgc")
   or TargetFileName == ".fullgc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
// Auditd via Syslog - fallback when ASIM not normalised
let SyslogHits = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Facility in ("user","auth","daemon","kern")
| where SyslogMessage has "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
  or (SyslogMessage has ".fullgc" and SyslogMessage has_any ("open","creat","chmod"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername="", EventType="FileCreated", TargetFilePath=SyslogMessage, TargetFileName=".fullgc", TargetFileSHA256="", ActingProcessName=ProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage;
union FileHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Qinglong .fullgc cryptominer execution with nohup backgrounding AIInstallation High
Detects execution of the .fullgc binary from /ql/data/db/, especially when launched with `nohup` and stdout/stderr suppressed (`>/dev/null 2>&1 &`) - the article's exact persistence-launch pattern. Pairs the masqueraded binary name with the article's verbatim launch command. Rationale: Triple-anchor on article-verbatim strings: (1) the binary name `.fullgc` (Code Block 1), (2) the absolute path `/ql/data/db/.fullgc` (Block snippet `b="/ql/data/db/.fullgc"`), and (3) the launch pattern `nohup "$b" >/dev/null 2>&1 &` (Block snippet). Filename was deliberately chosen to mimic JVM Full GC; the dot-prefix hides from `ls`; the path piggybacks on Qinglong's own data dir. Each anchor is high-fidelity on its own; combined they're near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2923 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2928 • https://github.com/whyour/qinglong/issues/2926
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1496 T1036.005 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR engineer detonating the recovered binary in a sandbox for analysis
  • Detection-validation lab launching a benign placeholder named .fullgc
  • Honeypot deliberately running the cryptominer to map C2
  • Backup snapshot of a previously-infected host being booted in restore-test mode
Suppression filter
// Defender - drop sandbox/IR detonations
| where DeviceName !in~ ("sandbox01","sandbox02","ir-detonation-vm")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("sandbox","ir-team","detection-eng")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull SHA256 + MD5 from DeviceProcessEvents, hash-match against VT/Intezer; confirm the host is a Qinglong instance; check CPU utilisation (article notes 85-100% sustained spike). Step 2 (contain): kill the .fullgc PID(s), quarantine `/ql/data/db/.fullgc`, snapshot the host for IR, sever outbound to file.551911.xyz at the perimeter, upgrade Qinglong past PR #2941, rotate all credentials stored in the panel, restore `/ql/config/config.sh` from a known-good source. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the binary SHA256 across the estate; check Nezha monitoring panels for the same C2 / file path (article-confirmed lateral pivot via Nezha); audit cron tasks (`/ql/data/db/cron.db`) for attacker-added jobs that re-launch the miner; alert on any future process write to /ql/data/db with the dot-prefix pattern as persistence regrowth.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName == ".fullgc")
   or FolderPath endswith "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or ProcessCommandLine has "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nohup") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)nohup\s+[\"']?[^\s]*\.fullgc")
| extend OutputSuppressed = tostring(ProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1"
| extend Backgrounded = tostring(ProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"&\s*$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, OutputSuppressed, Backgrounded
| order by Timestamp desc
// Primary: ASIM process events (Linux MDE, auditbeat, Sysmon-for-Linux normalised)
let AsimHits = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (ActingProcessName == ".fullgc")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has "/ql/data/db/.fullgc"
   or (ParentProcessName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nohup") and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)nohup\s+[\"']?[^\s]*\.fullgc")
| extend OutputSuppressed = tostring(ActingProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1"
| extend Backgrounded = tostring(ActingProcessCommandLine) matches regex @"&\s*$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256, OutputSuppressed, Backgrounded;
// Secondary: raw Syslog auditd EXECVE for non-MDE Linux hosts
let SyslogHits = Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/ql/data/db/.fullgc"," .fullgc ")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("EXECVE","execve","type=EXECVE","nohup")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname=Computer, ActorUsername="", ActingProcessName=".fullgc", ActingProcessCommandLine=SyslogMessage, ParentProcessName=ProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine="", SHA256="", OutputSuppressed=tostring(SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)>\s*/dev/null\s+2>&1"), Backgrounded=tostring(SyslogMessage matches regex @"&\s*$");
union AsimHits, SyslogHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects execution of the .fullgc cryptominer binary from /ql/data/db/, especially when launched via the article's verbatim nohup + suppressed-output + backgrounded pattern (`nohup "$b" >/dev/null 2>&1 &`). Filename masquerades as JVM Full GC.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/qinglong-task-scheduler-rce-vulnerabilities/

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.executable.path:*\/ql\/data\/db\/\.fullgc OR @process.executable.path:*\/\.fullgc OR @process.command_line:*\/ql\/data\/db\/\.fullgc* OR @process.command_line:*nohup*\.fullgc*)

Detected

Detected

Installation
Detected

Command & Control
Detected
Phase 7
Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] First-time OAuth consent granting Drive/Mail read scope to non-sanctioned third-party app · [LLM] Roblox cheat/exploit download on enterprise endpoint (Lumma Stealer entry vector) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Context.ai compromised Chrome extension installed on host (ID omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Cyberhaven compromised Chrome extension C2 callback (cyberhavenext.pro)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Cyberhaven compromised Chrome extension C2 callback (cyberhavenext.pro) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for network/DNS connections to the C2 infrastructure used by the malicious Cyberhaven Chrome extension update pushed Dec 25-26 2024 — the supply-chain incident the article cites. Looks for the C2 domain and its two Vultr-hosted IPs across all endpoints (180-day retrospective hunt, given the campaign hit multiple extensions and tokens may still be replayed). Rationale: C2 domain cyberhavenext.pro and hosting IPs 149.28.124.84 / 45.76.225.148 (AS20473 VULTR) are confirmed across Cyberhaven's own incident post, Sekoia's campaign writeup, and SOCRadar — all three corroborate the same infrastructure. The article (Aikido) explicitly anchors to this incident as one of the two named examples. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cyberhaven.com/blog/cyberhavens-chrome-extension-security-incident-and-what-were-doing-about-it • https://blog.sekoia.io/targeted-supply-chain-attack-against-chrome-browser-extensions/ • https://socradar.io/blog/phishing-attack-cyberhaven-chrome-extension/ • https://www.hunters.security/en/blog/chrome-extension-threat-campaign
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1195.002 T1539
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst VM intentionally resolving the IOC from a sandbox
  • Security vendor product (EDR, NDR) emitting the IOC as a test/canary against itself
  • Historic Cyberhaven extension version reaching out before being patched — confirm extension is updated
  • Honeypot or deception platform configured to bait the same C2
  • Public DNS resolver that logged-but-didn't-route the query (informational, not an actual host callout)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe") == false and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","sentinel-ti","ti-vm")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--headless","--ti-canary"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pivot on Device/SrcHostname and pull all DeviceNetworkEvents to those IPs in the past 30 days plus the InitiatingProcess that made the call; verify Cyberhaven extension version installed (chrome://extensions). 2) Contain — isolate the endpoint, force-uninstall the Cyberhaven extension, revoke all browser cookies & Workspace OAuth grants for the user (Google Admin → Security → API controls → Manage Third-Party App Access), rotate the user's SaaS session tokens (Slack, Notion, GitHub). 3) Hunt — run UC2 (Context.ai extension ID) across the fleet, search 180-day proxy/Zeek logs for the same domain/IPs from any host, and check for additional compromised extension IDs from the Sekoia/Hunters campaign list (e.g. nrcicnlhnodlqocnkpgijckbidfdkidf, fbmlbgooljkjhdgfgjblapehpdgmjelb).
let BadDomains = dynamic(["cyberhavenext.pro"]);
let BadIPs = dynamic(["149.28.124.84","45.76.225.148"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (BadDomains) or RemoteIP in (BadIPs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadDomains = dynamic(["cyberhavenext.pro"]);
let BadIPs = dynamic(["149.28.124.84","45.76.225.148"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImNetworkSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
 | where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs) or DstHostname has_any (BadDomains) or Url has_any (BadDomains)
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
 | where DnsQuery has_any (BadDomains)
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cyberhaven Compromised Chrome Extension C2 Callback
id: 6b8d5e02-3f5e-4f1d-9a3c-1c1a8a2b9f10
description: Detects network traffic to the C2 infrastructure used by the malicious Cyberhaven Chrome extension update (Dec 25-26 2024 supply-chain compromise).
references:
  - https://www.cyberhaven.com/blog/cyberhavens-chrome-extension-security-incident-and-what-were-doing-about-it
  - https://blog.sekoia.io/targeted-supply-chain-attack-against-chrome-browser-extensions/
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/browser-extensions-supply-chain-attack
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1539
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_domain:
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'cyberhavenext.pro'
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp:
      - '149.28.124.84'
      - '45.76.225.148'
  condition: selection_domain or selection_ip
falsepositives:
  - Threat-intel research VMs intentionally pulling the IOC
level: high
(source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.syslog OR cloudtrail) AND ((@EventID:3 AND (@DestinationIp:(149.28.124.84 OR 45.76.225.148) OR @DestinationHostname:(*cyberhavenext.pro* OR *CyberhavenExt.pro*))) OR (@EventID:22 AND @QueryName:(*cyberhavenext.pro* OR *CyberhavenExt.pro*)) OR (@network.destination.ip:(149.28.124.84 OR 45.76.225.148))))
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/cyberhavenext\.pro$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=/^(149\.28\.124\.84|45\.76\.225\.148)$/)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest in ("149.28.124.84","45.76.225.148") OR All_Traffic.dest_host="cyberhavenext.pro" OR like(All_Traffic.dest_host,"%.cyberhavenext.pro")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | append [ | tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*cyberhavenext.pro" by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest in ("149.28.124.84","45.76.225.148") OR All_Traffic.dest_host="cyberhavenext.pro" OR like(All_Traffic.dest_host,"%.cyberhavenext.pro")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | append [ | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*cyberhavenext.pro" by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ]
Context.ai compromised Chrome extension installed on host (ID omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk) AIInstallation High
Hunts for the file artefacts of the Context.ai Chrome extension that was removed from the Chrome Web Store on 2026-03-27 after the Lumma-Stealer-driven OAuth token theft that fed the Vercel breach. Detects the extension's installation directory on Chrome user-data paths — the only reliable on-host signal since silent auto-update can re-install it the next time Chrome syncs. Rationale: Extension ID omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk is confirmed by Vercel's own incident bulletin, The Hacker News, ox.security, and Push Security as the Context.ai Chrome extension removed from the Web Store 2026-03-27. Chrome stores extensions in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\<Profile>\Extensions\<extID>\`, so a file-path match on the ID is a deterministic on-host signal regardless of whether the extension is currently enabled. Cross-checked against: • https://vercel.com/kb/bulletin/vercel-april-2026-security-incident • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/vercel-breach-tied-to-context-ai-hack.html • https://www.ox.security/blog/vercel-context-ai-supply-chain-attack-breachforums/ • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/unpacking-the-vercel-breach
ATT&CKT1176 T1195.002 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR/forensic workstation with a captured Chrome profile staged for analysis
  • Endpoint formerly running the extension before Google's 2026-03-27 takedown — confirm last-modified timestamp is pre-takedown
  • Security tool quarantine bucket storing the extension files post-removal
  • Threat-intel researcher detonating the extension in a sandbox VM
  • Backup/imaging tool replicating an old user profile that contained the extension
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","ir-","forensic")) and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Quarantine\\","\\Backup\\","\\Image\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — for each hit, pull the extension's manifest.json file event to determine first-installed time and the user profile; cross-check whether that user ever signed into Google Workspace from this host. 2) Contain — uninstall the extension (`chrome://extensions/?id=omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk` or push GPO/Endpoint Manager force-uninstall), revoke the user's Google Workspace OAuth grants for Context.ai in Google Admin Console, rotate any Drive-stored secrets (env files, API keys, NPM/GitHub tokens) the user had Drive access to. 3) Hunt — pivot to UC3 (high-risk OAuth grants) for the same user, audit Drive Activity API for mass downloads in the 30 days before takedown, and check downstream PaaS (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare) audit logs for token reuse from non-corporate IPs.
let ExtId = "omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk";
union
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
 | where FolderPath has ExtId
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath),
(DeviceProcessEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(180d)
 | where ProcessCommandLine has ExtId
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Evidence=make_set(strcat(FileName, " :: ", FolderPath), 10)
  by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by FirstSeen asc
let ExtId = "omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk";
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where TargetFilePath has ExtId
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), FileCount=count(), SampleFile=any(TargetFileName)
  by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName
| order by FirstSeen asc

id: 7b1cae20-5a3c-4d4f-bc2e-2c6dac4d1a40
description: Detects the on-disk presence of the malicious Context.ai Chrome extension (ID omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk) removed from the Chrome Web Store on 2026-03-27 after the Vercel OAuth supply-chain breach.

  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/vercel-breach-tied-to-context-ai-hack.html

((source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:11 AND @TargetFilename:*omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk*) OR (source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:1 AND @CommandLine:*omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk*) OR (source:linux.auditd AND @file.path:*omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk*))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk/i) OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk/i) OR (#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegStringValue=/omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk/i)

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\*\\Extensions\\omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\*\\Sync Extension Settings\\omddlmnhcofjbnbflmjginpjjblphbgk*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

First-time OAuth consent granting Drive/Mail read scope to non-sanctioned third-party app AIDelivery Medium
Detects the consent step that the article identifies as the supply-chain entry point — an employee granting a browser extension or SaaS app OAuth permissions broad enough that one compromise of the vendor cascades into the org's Workspace/M365 data. Targets new third-party app consents with file/mail/offline_access scopes by users who have not previously granted that level of trust. Rationale: Article's central thesis is that broad OAuth scopes granted to third-party extensions create the supply-chain pivot — explicitly: 'highly privileged OAuth token was sitting in Context.ai's AWS backend.' The Push Security and Trend Micro writeups both confirm the consent step (Drive read scope on the Chrome extension) as the pivot. Detecting first-time consent to risky scopes catches the dangerous grant before the vendor is compromised, which is the only proactive window. Cross-checked against: • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/unpacking-the-vercel-breach • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/d/vercel-breach-oauth-supply-chain.html • https://venturebeat.com/security/vercel-breach-exposes-the-oauth-gap-most-security-teams-cannot-detect-scope-or-contain • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
ATT&CKT1528 T1550.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT-sanctioned new SaaS rollout (e.g. new Slack/Notion/Salesforce integration) granting Mail/Drive scopes legitimately
  • Microsoft Graph PowerShell or admin-consent flow done by IT staff at change-window
  • User re-consenting to an already-trusted app after a scope upgrade
  • Marketing/HR vendor integrations like DocuSign or Greenhouse that need offline_access
  • Pen-test or red-team OAuth consent simulation
Suppression filter
| where InitiatorUPN !in~ ("admin@contoso.com","global-admin@contoso.com") and AppName !in~ (dynamic(["Slack","DocuSign","Notion","Salesforce","GitHub","Greenhouse"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage — open the Entra Enterprise Apps blade for the AppName, check publisher verification status, total tenant grants, and whether the app is on the org's allowlist; query AuditLogs for the same AppId across all users to see consent fan-out. 2) Contain — if unsanctioned, revoke the OAuth2PermissionGrant via Graph (`Remove-MgOauth2PermissionGrant`) and force a token revocation for the user; block the app at tenant level (Enterprise Apps → Properties → Enabled for users = No). 3) Hunt — pivot on the AppId in MailItemsAccessed / OfficeActivity / Graph audit logs to inventory what data the token already accessed, check downstream SaaS for the same user signing in from non-corporate IPs in the consent window, and review Conditional Access policies for an admin-consent-required rule on high-risk scopes.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in~ ("Consent to application", "Add app role assignment grant to user", "Add delegated permission grant to user")
| extend Raw = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend AppName = tostring(Raw.Target[0].ID)
| extend ModProps = Raw.ModifiedProperties
| extend ScopeText = tostring(ModProps)
| where ScopeText has_any ("Files.Read","Files.ReadWrite","Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Sites.Read.All","offline_access","googleapis.com/auth/drive","googleapis.com/auth/documents")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), GrantCount=count() by AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, AppName, IPAddress, CountryCode
| where FirstSeen > ago(7d)
| order by FirstSeen desc
let RiskyScopes = dynamic(["Files.Read","Files.ReadWrite","Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Sites.Read.All","offline_access","googleapis.com/auth/drive","googleapis.com/auth/documents","googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets"]);
let Recent = AuditLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where OperationName in~ ("Consent to application","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant","Add delegated permission grant","Add app role assignment grant to user")
    | extend InitiatorUPN = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
    | mv-expand TargetResources
    | extend AppName = tostring(TargetResources.displayName)
    | extend ModProps = TargetResources.modifiedProperties
    | mv-expand ModProps
    | extend NewValue = tostring(ModProps.newValue)
    | where NewValue has_any (RiskyScopes);
let Baseline = AuditLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(90d) .. ago(7d))
    | where OperationName in~ ("Consent to application","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant","Add delegated permission grant")
    | extend InitiatorUPN = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
    | mv-expand TargetResources
    | extend AppName = tostring(TargetResources.displayName)
    | distinct InitiatorUPN, AppName;
Recent
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on InitiatorUPN, AppName
| project TimeGenerated, InitiatorUPN, AppName, NewValue, Result, CorrelationId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: First-Time OAuth Consent With Drive/Mail/Offline Scope to Third-Party App
id: 8f3acb91-2ce4-4f0c-bd23-9ab5f3c0fa18
description: Detects a user granting consent to a third-party application requesting broad Mail/Drive/offline_access OAuth scopes — the consent step that fed the Context.ai-Vercel supply-chain compromise.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/browser-extensions-supply-chain-attack
  - https://pushsecurity.com/blog/unpacking-the-vercel-breach
  - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/d/vercel-breach-oauth-supply-chain.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.t1550.001
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection_op:
    OperationName:
      - 'Consent to application'
      - 'Add OAuth2PermissionGrant'
      - 'Add delegated permission grant'
  selection_scope:
    TargetResources|contains:
      - 'Files.Read'
      - 'Files.ReadWrite'
      - 'Mail.Read'
      - 'Mail.ReadWrite'
      - 'Sites.Read.All'
      - 'offline_access'
      - 'googleapis.com/auth/drive'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned enterprise apps newly approved by IT
  - Admin-consent flow performed by Global Administrator on behalf of users
level: medium
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Consent to application" OR "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant" OR "Add delegated permission grant") @properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties.newValue:(*Files.Read* OR *Files.ReadWrite* OR *Mail.Read* OR *Mail.ReadWrite* OR *Sites.Read.All* OR *offline_access* OR *googleapis.com\/auth\/drive* OR *googleapis.com\/auth\/documents*)
#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog OperationName=/(Consent to application|Add OAuth2PermissionGrant|Add delegated permission grant)/i
| regex("(Files\\.Read|Files\\.ReadWrite|Mail\\.Read|Sites\\.Read\\.All|offline_access|googleapis\\.com/auth/drive)", field=ModifiedProperties)
| groupBy([UserPrincipalName, AppName], function=[min(_time, as=FirstSeen), count(as=Grants)])
| sort(FirstSeen, order=desc)
CLOUD
`azure_audit_logs` (OperationName="Consent to application" OR OperationName="Add OAuth2PermissionGrant" OR OperationName="Add delegated permission grant")
| spath output=AppName path="TargetResources{}.displayName"
| spath output=ConsentValues path="TargetResources{}.modifiedProperties{}.newValue"
| eval Scopes=mvjoin(ConsentValues,",")
| search Scopes IN ("*Files.Read*","*Files.ReadWrite*","*Mail.Read*","*Mail.ReadWrite*","*Sites.Read.All*","*offline_access*","*https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive*")
| spath output=Initiator path="InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName"
| stats min(_time) as firstSeen count by Initiator AppName Scopes
| eventstats values(AppName) as KnownApps by Initiator
| where firstSeen > relative_time(now(), "-7d@d")
| convert ctime(firstSeen)
Roblox cheat/exploit download on enterprise endpoint (Lumma Stealer entry vector) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for downloads of Roblox executors and 'auto-farm' scripts to corporate endpoints — the exact initial-access vector the article attributes to the Context.ai employee's Lumma Stealer infection that fed the Vercel breach. Pairs file-name patterns of known Roblox cheat tools with download paths and known distribution hosts. Rationale: The Hacker News, Reco.ai, and Push Security writeups all corroborate the article's claim that the Context.ai employee was Lumma-Stealer-infected via Roblox 'auto-farm' / executor downloads in Feb 2026 — making this the documented initial-access vector. The cheat-tool family names (Synapse X, Krnl, Fluxus, Hydrogen, Wave) and their distribution hosts are stable IOCs across MalwareBazaar and ThreatFox listings for Lumma droppers. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/vercel-breach-tied-to-context-ai-hack.html • https://www.reco.ai/blog/vercel-context-ai-breach • https://pushsecurity.com/blog/unpacking-the-vercel-breach • https://tech-insider.org/vercel-breach-shinyhunters-oauth-context-ai-2026/
ATT&CKT1189 T1204.002 T1566
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer at a game/Roblox-adjacent studio legitimately working with the names 'synapse' or 'hydrogen' (both also Python/React libraries respectively)
  • Malware analyst sandbox VM detonating Lumma lures intentionally
  • Penetration test simulating the attack chain
  • User naming a project folder 'auto-farm' for crop/agtech automation
  • Security tool quarantine path retaining the file after blocked download
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detonation","malware-lab","redteam")) and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("7zfm.exe","winrar.exe") and FolderPath has "\\malware-samples\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the InitiatingProcess and FileOriginUrl for the file event; if browser-originated, check DeviceNetworkEvents for the user's full download chain and any subsequent process executions from %TEMP% within 30 minutes. 2) Contain — isolate the host (Defender Device Isolation or Falcon RTR network-contain), block the download domain at proxy, force user re-authentication and revoke all browser cookies + corporate SaaS sessions for that account, rotate any keys in env files / pass-managers the user could access. 3) Hunt — search 30-day DeviceFileEvents for the same FileHash on other hosts, run Defender's Lumma Stealer playbook (clipboard.dat, %APPDATA%\Roaming\* exfil staging), and pivot to UC3 to see whether the user granted any risky OAuth scopes that the stealer could have lifted.
let CheatNames = dynamic(["synapse","krnl","fluxus","hydrogen","argon","wave_executor","wave-executor","autofarm","auto-farm","roblox-exploit","robloxexploit","roblox_bypass"]);
let CheatHosts = dynamic(["wearedevs.net","krnl.cat","krnl.place","krnl.live","fluxteam.net","synapsex.to","hydrogenwave.com","getsynapse.cc"]);
union
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where FolderPath has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Desktop\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")
 | where FileName has_any (CheatNames)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginIP),
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
 | where RemoteUrl has_any (CheatHosts)
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP)
| order by Timestamp desc
let CheatNames = dynamic(["synapse","krnl","fluxus","hydrogen","argon","wave_executor","wave-executor","autofarm","auto-farm","roblox-exploit","robloxexploit"]);

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,

| order by Timestamp desc

| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

| order by files desc

DeviceEvents

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

fast16 Sabotage Framework Hash IOC Sweep (svcmgmt.exe / fast16.sys / svcmgmt.dll) AIInstallation High
Sweeps endpoint file, process and image-load telemetry for the eight SHA256 hashes published by SentinelLABS for the fast16 sabotage framework — the svcmgmt.exe Lua-VM carrier, the fast16.sys boot-start filesystem driver, and the svcmgmt.dll RAS connotify reporter. High-fidelity because these hashes belong to one disclosed campaign and are not present in benign software inventories. Rationale: Uses the eight SHA256 / SHA1 / MD5 hashes published by SentinelLABS for the disclosed fast16 framework components (svcmgmt.exe carrier, fast16.sys driver, svcmgmt.dll connotify DLL) plus the additional samples in the IOC table. Hashes are immutable per-binary identifiers — any match is high confidence. As of the article's publication (2026-04-23) and 12 days later, no second-source vendor write-up is yet public; ShipShape would normally cite Mandiant/CrowdStrike/MSRC corroboration but here the IOCs come from a single primary disclosure — flag for re-validation once external sources publish.
ATT&CKT1014 T1543.003 T1565.001

title: fast16 Sabotage Framework Binary Execution by Hash
id: 8c4d2e1a-7b3f-4a92-bc56-fa57167a5616
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of binaries belonging to the fast16 sabotage framework disclosed by SentinelLABS — the svcmgmt.exe Lua-VM carrier (2005-08-30 build), the fast16.sys boot-start filesystem driver (2005-07-19 build), and the svcmgmt.dll RAS connotify reporter (2005-06-06 build) — by SHA256 hash. Referenced in the ShadowBrokers Territorial Dispute drv_list.txt deconfliction file.
references:
    - https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/fast16-mystery-shadowbrokers-reference-reveals-high-precision-software-sabotage-5-years-before-stuxnet/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/05
tags:
    - attack.t1014
    - attack.t1543.003
    - attack.t1565.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows

fast16 Carrier Runtime Artefacts (SvcMgmt service / pipe p577 / \Device\fast16) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for the runtime fingerprint left by the fast16 carrier and kernel driver: a Windows service named 'SvcMgmt' pointing at svcmgmt.exe, a named pipe '\\.\pipe\p577' opened by the connotify DLL, the registration of a kernel device '\Device\fast16' / '\??\fast16', and registry persistence at 'PrefetchParameters\EnablePrefetcher=0' performed by the driver entry point. Catches a re-deployed or modernised variant even when hashes have been recompiled. Rationale: Anchored on four article-specific runtime strings that don't appear together by chance: (1) Windows service name 'SvcMgmt' as named in the carrier installer code-path, (2) named pipe '\\.\pipe\p577' decoded by svcmgmt.dll connotify DLL, (3) device object '\Device\fast16' / '\??\fast16' registered by fast16.sys, and (4) the driver's first action of zeroing 'EnablePrefetcher' under PrefetchParameters. Sigma omitted because the detection unions multiple log categories (file_event + registry_event + service install + named pipe). No external corroboration available 12 days post-disclosure.
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1014 T1112 T1564
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry Endpoint.Services
let _fast16_files = dynamic(["svcmgmt.exe","svcmgmt.dll","fast16.sys"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  ( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where FileName in~ (_fast16_files)
       or FolderPath has @"\Device\fast16"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource=strcat("File:", ActionType), Detail=strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName), SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName ),
  ( DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "NamedPipeEvent"
    | where FileName has "p577" or AdditionalFields has "p577" or AdditionalFields has @"\\.\pipe\p577"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource="NamedPipe", Detail=tostring(coalesce(FileName, AdditionalFields)), SHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName ),
  ( DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("DriverLoad","ServiceInstalled")
    | where FileName in~ (_fast16_files) or FolderPath has @"fast16" or RegistryValueName has "SvcMgmt" or RegistryValueData has "svcmgmt.exe" or RegistryValueData has "fast16.sys"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource=ActionType, Detail=strcat(coalesce(FolderPath,""), "\\", coalesce(FileName,""), " reg=", coalesce(RegistryValueData,"")), SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName ),
  ( DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where (RegistryKey has @"\Services\SvcMgmt")
         or (RegistryKey has @"\Session Manager\Memory Management\PrefetchParameters" and RegistryValueName =~ "EnablePrefetcher" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryValueData has "svcmgmt.exe" or RegistryValueData has "fast16.sys")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventSource=strcat("Registry:", ActionType), Detail=strcat(RegistryKey, " ", RegistryValueName, "=", RegistryValueData), SHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName )
| summarize HitCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Sources=make_set(EventSource), Details=make_set(Detail, 20) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where HitCount >= 1
| order by LastSeen desc
let _fast16_files = dynamic(["svcmgmt.exe","svcmgmt.dll","fast16.sys"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  ( ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where TargetFileName in~ (_fast16_files) or TargetFilePath has @"\Device\fast16"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, EventSource=strcat("File:", EventType), Detail=TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername ),
  ( ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where (RegistryKey has @"\Services\SvcMgmt")
         or (RegistryKey has @"\Session Manager\Memory Management\PrefetchParameters" and RegistryValue =~ "EnablePrefetcher" and tostring(RegistryValueData) == "0")
         or (tostring(RegistryValueData) has "svcmgmt.exe" or tostring(RegistryValueData) has "fast16.sys")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, EventSource="Registry", Detail=strcat(RegistryKey, " ", RegistryValue, "=", tostring(RegistryValueData)), ActingProcessName, ActorUsername ),
  ( SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EventID == 4697
    | where ServiceName has "SvcMgmt" or ServiceFileName has "svcmgmt.exe" or ServiceFileName has "fast16.sys"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventSource="ServiceInstalled-4697", Detail=strcat(ServiceName, " -> ", ServiceFileName, " start=", ServiceStartType), ActingProcessName=ProcessName, ActorUsername=SubjectUserName ),
  ( WindowsEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
    | where EventID in (17, 18)
    | extend PipeName = tostring(EventData.PipeName), Image = tostring(EventData.Image)
    | where PipeName has "p577" or PipeName has @"\\.\pipe\p577"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventSource="NamedPipe-Sysmon", Detail=strcat(PipeName, " by ", Image), ActingProcessName=Image, ActorUsername=tostring(EventData.User) ),
  ( WindowsEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
    | where EventID == 6
    | extend ImageLoaded = tostring(EventData.ImageLoaded), Hashes = tostring(EventData.Hashes)
    | where ImageLoaded has "fast16" or ImageLoaded has "svcmgmt"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventSource="DriverLoad-Sysmon6", Detail=strcat(ImageLoaded, " ", Hashes), ActingProcessName=ImageLoaded, ActorUsername="" )
| summarize HitCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sources=make_set(EventSource), Details=make_set(Detail, 20) by Computer, ActingProcessName, ActorUsername
| where HitCount >= 1
| order by LastSeen desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
